title: Southern Catalpa: Old Catalpas You Can Visit
meta_description: The trumpet tree of the American southeast, and it rarely grows straight. In Baarn, Queen Juliana told her gardener to leave a fallen one where it lay.
intro: Old catalpas rarely grow straight, and Dutch gardeners have learned to let them. In April 1973 a storm knocked one flat in the grounds of Paleis Soestdijk in Baarn, and Queen Juliana told her gardener to leave it where it fell; new trunks have risen along its length since. Deventer's at De Lathmer has gone horizontal with age and lies across the grass, still flowering every summer. Breda's leans so far out over the pond in Wilhelminapark that the municipality props its lowest limbs on columns, and Milan's has spent about 136 years twisting behind a baroque fish pond in the Giardini della Guastalla. The species comes from a small pocket of the southeastern United States and is far commoner in European gardens than at home. It is bare well into May, then hangs out speckled cream trumpets in July and long thin pods after.
